items.title: Anil Agarwal warns Vedanta block transfer to ONGC could deter investors
items.summary:
Mining czar Anil Agarwal on Tuesday warned that the government's decision to transfer operations of a producing offshore oil and gas block from his company to state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) could send wrong signal to investors.
In a LinkedIn post, he urged policymakers to maintain regulatory stability and avoid disrupting existing operators.
"Recently, our running field has been given to ONGC which will send a very wrong signal to investors," he said, referring to the disputed Cambay offshore block in Gujarat that ONGC took over from Vedanta in July following a Delhi High Court ruling.
Agarwal said Vedanta Oil and Gas, which he described as India's largest private-sector producer, was committing USD 5 billion to scale up production to between 300,000 and 500,000 barrels per day. He did not indicate a timeline for reaching the production.

Speaking on the role of AI in life sciences, Shaw, the Executive Chairperson, Biocon Ltd, noted that accelerating this journey from lab to clinic will unlock major opportunities in precision and personalised medicine.
"Ultimately the process of drug development doesn't end in the labs. It has to be validated in clinical trials. How do you pick the right patients? How do you conduct these trials in a way that gives you early readouts?

Belrise Industries shares jump 11% as Q2 profit rises 25% YoY; revenue grows 17%
items.summary: Belrise Industries shares rallied 10.50% to Rs 237.78 during Monday’s trading session after the company reported 25% year-on-year (YoY) growth in profit after tax (PAT) and a 17% increase in revenue from operations for the September quarter (Q2 FY27).Belrise Industries Limited (BIL), an integrated automotive component manufacturer, announced its financial results for Q2 FY27 and the first half of FY27, reporting growth in both revenue and profitability.The company's revenue from operations increased 17% YoY to Rs 2,746 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,353 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Profit after tax (PAT) rose 25% to Rs 166 crore from Rs 133 crore in Q2 FY26.Belrise Industries Q2 FY27 business highlightsThe company's manufacturing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 23,441 million in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 18,601 million in the year-ago quarter. Manufacturing EBITDA increased 19% to Rs 3,170 million from Rs 2,663 million in Q2 FY26. Manufacturing EBITDA margin stood at 13.5% during the quarter. Additionally, 71% of the company's manufacturing revenue came from powertrain-neutral products.Belrise Industries H1 FY27 performanceFor the first half of FY27, manufacturing revenue increased 23% YoY to Rs 45,420 million, compared with Rs 36,923 million in H1 FY26. Manufacturing EBITDA rose 15% to Rs 5,963 million from Rs 5,199 million in the corresponding period last year. The manufacturing EBITDA margin stood at 13.1%, while powertrain-neutral products accounted for 71% of manufacturing revenue.Belrise Industries secures new ordersDuring the quarter, Belrise Industries secured several new orders across its commercial vehicle and two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses. The company won a programme from a leading Indian commercial vehicle manufacturer to supply complete chassis frame assemblies across its heavy commercial vehicle (HCV) platforms. The supplies will be made from a new facility in Dharwad, with production expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28.The programme is expected to add Rs 60,000–1 lakh in content per vehicle, with peak annual revenue potential of Rs 1,500–2,000 million.Belrise also entered complete three-wheeler body manufacturing after being selected as the second source for complete body and chassis assemblies for a high-selling model of a leading Indian two-wheeler and three-wheeler manufacturer. The order represents incremental content of approximately Rs 9,000 per vehicle.Production from its new facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28, with peak annual revenue potential of Rs 1,000–1,200 million.In its suspension business, the company onboarded its sixth original equipment manufacturer (OEM) customer, a leading premium two-wheeler manufacturer in South India. Supplies commenced in Q3 FY27. It also secured additional orders from a growing two-wheeler and three-wheeler OEM, with production expected to begin in Q4 FY27.What management saidCommenting on the company's Q2 and H1 FY27 performance, Shrikant Badve, Managing Director of Belrise Industries, said the quarter was marked by strong execution and a healthy demand environment. He highlighted that manufacturing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 23,441 million, while adjusted PAT increased 25% to Rs 1,663 million.Also read: Tata Motors PV shares crack 9% as Motilal Oswal cuts earnings estimates, stays bearish after Q2 resultsThe company also secured its maiden Letter of Intent (LoI) for the supply of CNC fixtures to an ecosystem partner of one of the largest American smartphone companies.According to Badve, India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem is poised to become one of the country's largest and most cost-competitive manufacturing segments. The new order will provide Belrise with an opportunity to demonstrate its precision engineering capabilities developed over the years.Share PriceBelrise Industries shares have rallied 45% over the past one year. The stock is currently trading at a market capitalisation of Rs 21,567 crore. ONGC takes over disputed Cambay block from Vedanta after court ruling
items.summary:
State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore block from Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies.
Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd has recognised an impairment charge of about Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block.
The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on July 22, 2026, after the High Court's single-judge bench dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing.
The block was operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest; ONGC held 50 per cent, and Invenire Petrodyne Ltd had the remaining 10 per cent.
The government, through a September 19, 2025, letter, declined to extend the contract and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC.
Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court
